summary: Earth Jukebox is a web app that turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into sound. Each image is loaded into a binary partition tree, the whole image is the root, and any region with high color variation is split in half, alternating vertical and horizontal cuts, until regions are uniform or small. Each leaf stores its average color. A traversal of the tree (preorder, inorder, postorder or level order) places the leaves in a queue, and an audio player dequeues them one by one, playing a note per region: cooler colors sound lower, warmer colors higher, larger regions last longer and louder, and position pans the sound left to right. Smooth areas like open ocean become long notes; detailed areas become many short ones. The interface highlights the region being played and provides text descriptions, keyboard shortcuts and screen-reader support. This makes complex Earth science accessible to blind and low-vision users and gives everyone a new, multi-sensory way to explore our changing planet.
details:
Earth Jukebox turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into sound. The image becomes the root of a binary tree: any region with high color variation is split in half, alternating vertical and horizontal cuts, until regions are uniform or small. Each leaf stores its average color. A tree traversal places the leaves in a queue, and an audio player plays one note per region: cooler colors sound lower, warmer colors higher, larger regions last longer and louder, and position sets stereo pan. A slider controls the level of detail.

It makes Earth science accessible to blind and low-vision users, with text descriptions, keyboard shortcuts and screen-reader support, and lets everyone hear patterns in the data. We used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, the Canvas and Web Audio APIs, Node.js for tests, and GitHub Pages. The tree and queue are implemented from scratch. It is creative because the data structure itself shapes the music: smooth areas become long notes and detailed areas become many short ones, on a pentatonic scale so the result stays pleasant.
